sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Mahendra Realtors is principally a structural-repair, rehabilitation, waterproofing and civil-works contractor, with legacy BOT/property exposures. It is not a conventional land-bank developer. The attractive surface story is a profitable contractor at about 7.1× FY26 profit and roughly book value. The decisive problem is that much of the apparent cash is project collateral, multi-year cash conversion is weak, and important notes do not reconcile. BQS is 4.5 and capped GQS 5.0; IAS is NS. This is a conditional value/special-situation research case, not an evidence-backed compounder or an eligible new-purchase recommendation. A clear auditor reconciliation, freely usable liquidity and demonstrably collectible contract assets would change the conclusion more than a lower headline P/E. [E01,E06,E07,E11,E22]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Research cutoff: 20 October 2026, India market information; prepared after the cutoff without incorporating later economic events. Legal security: Mahendra Realtors & Infrastructure Limited, MRIL, ISIN INE632Q01018, NSE Emerge. The last authenticated issuer trade is ₹57 on 15 October, two scheduled sessions stale at the 19 October reference; 20 October was an exchange holiday. Issued shares are 22,103,900, giving ₹125.99 crore market capitalization. Scope is standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards (AS) under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, not an assumed Ind AS consolidation. No subsidiary/associate was reported in FY26; a 50% partnership investment and proposed JV are separate exposures. Horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with actual-day return calculation and 15% nominal pretax INR hurdle. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is illustrative. G1 and G3 are Conditional; G2 and G4 are Hold—unresolved. Confidence is High on identity and the authenticated source values, Medium on historical operating growth/capital-return diagnostics, and Low on current free-cash reconciliation and ordinary valuation. A clean main opinion is not a substitute for resolving note inconsistencies. [E01,E07,E10,E11,E21]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The 13 canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. BQS raw/final is 4.52, displayed 4.5. GQS raw 5.20 is capped at 5.00 because persistent CASH 3 meets the stated growth-quality override, not because working capital expanded once. IAS has 45% factor-weight coverage: unrounded BQS contributes 1.13 and D contributes 0.60; 55% is missing. Its mathematical bound is 2.28–7.23, not a confidence interval or a point score. No neutral imputation or reweighting is used. CAP is scoreable from a reconciled multi-year aggregate bridge despite absent private project IRRs. GOV is 4, not≤3, because there is insufficient evidence of severe proven abuse. G2 reliability concerns prevent numerical quality/growth ranking even though their arithmetic is computable; all ranking flags are false. A one-point change in either GOV or CAP changes raw BQS by 0.20 or 0.12; jointly ±0.32. A one-point CAP change moves raw GQS 0.15, with its cap still separately applied. [E06,E10,E13,E20,E22]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company sells works-contract execution: structural repairs, restoration, retrofitting, waterproofing, interiors, plumbing, maintenance and civil construction. It wins and executes tenders, employs supervisors and subcontractors, procures materials and books engineer-certified progress. Profit becomes cash only after certification, billing, departmental approval and payment; retention/security money can remain blocked beyond completion and defect-liability periods. Project duration is usually 6–24 months, while the offer document describes roughly 12-month working-capital cycles and longer security lock-up. FY25 Maharashtra generated 96.55% of revenue; the largest customer 39.13% and top ten 81.29% make regional procurement and a few payment departments material. Main FY25/26 revenue is service revenue. FY23/24 also included BOT revenue of₹6.1870/0.8246 cr, so the mix is not perfectly constant. Rashta Peth BOT WIP₹3.7323 cr and Shirur balances have no FY26 revenue, and they are not treated as a separate growth engine. Waste-management and patent references are management claims without a separately evidenced recurring revenue stream; no optionality premium is assigned. [E01,E03,E04,E24]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The useful advantage is accumulated experience, technical teams, execution references and tender eligibility. These can reduce entry friction, but they do not establish durable pricing power. The offer document explicitly describes aggressive bids below estimated project costs requiring additional security. The July 2025 JNPA case illustrates that eligibility is specific: the company did not satisfy the required guniting experience for one cited project, and the court upheld technical disqualification without deciding separate misrepresentation allegations. Direct competing bidders in that tender, Painterior Protective Systems LLP and Shandar Interior Pvt Ltd, are more relevant operational comparators than residential developers; audited public multiples were not obtained for these unlisted firms. PSP Projects is a listed general-building contractor comparison, much larger and with a different project mix: its dated H1FY26 presentation showed 105 receivable days and 102 working-capital days, highlighting industry collection risk rather than excusing MRIL's own weakness. Innovators Facade Systems is a specialized facade-engineering comparator, not repair-only and not a justified identical multiple. No verified market-share denominator, lowest-cost benchmark or customer switching-cost study supports a higher moat score. [E03,E16,E23]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Five audited years FY22–26 are available through restatement and the latest annual report. Revenue moved₹92.66→63.02→101.49→124.77→135.86 cr. Annual changes were−₹29.64 cr, +₹38.47 cr, +₹23.28 cr and +₹11.09 cr. The selected five-year contextual CAGR is 14.92% from the rating agency's FY21 actual₹67.77 cr; the earlier original audit was not retrieved. Importantly, the fully audited four-interval FY22–26 CAGR 10.04% leads to the same starting REV 6. The three-year CAGR 29.18% starts at depressed FY23, so it is disclosed but not cherry-picked. FY26 growth slowed to 8.89% from 22.94%; a single annual comparison does not earn a separate trajectory adjustment. The perimeter is standalone with no identified acquisition driving the revenue increase, supporting an organic-execution interpretation, but contract volumes, rates, scope changes and inflation are not separately reconciled. FY23 BOT recognition and subsequent service mix also matter. No verified latest FY27 interim or comparable quarterly cash-flow series was found; no fabricated TTM or annualized seasonal quarter is used. Ten-year comparable growth remains ND. [E02,E05,E24]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Repair demand can persist as structures age, but accessible growth depends on tenders, qualified teams, client budgets, guarantees and collection capacity rather than physical plant utilization alone. The last dated backlog was₹193.41 cr on 31 July 2025, around 1.55× FY25 sales, not a current FY26 coverage ratio. There is no authenticated opening backlog + wins − execution − cancellations reconciliation. A bottom-up throughput check uses the rating agency's₹5–10 cr typical ticket: FY26 revenue represents roughly 14–27 full-ticket equivalents annually, not 14–27 disclosed completed projects. The base model reaches roughly₹220 cr annualized revenue near October 2031, requiring about 22–44 such equivalents, larger guarantee/security balances and additional net working capital. This is an analyst scenario, not a secured order schedule. Base operating EBITDA margin 14.5% is near FY26; no improvement from new waste or property operations is assumed. Both higher and lower collection/collateral intensities are tested. The capital bridge shows mixed 6–17% core incremental returns across windows, not persistently superior economics. Growth cannot be paid out as dividends while also funding receivables and guarantees. GQS 5.0 reflects genuine revenue progress limited by poor cash conversion, not lack of demand alone. [E04,E06,E20,E22]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Stewardship is mixed. Director remuneration rose₹2.10 cr in FY 23 to₹6.60 cr,₹7.95 cr and₹12.00 cr in FY 26; the latest amount is 67.62% of PAT. The auditor states Section 197 compliance, so this is an economic alignment concern, not an asserted statutory breach. Disclosed related commercial services and loans are retained in costs/obligations; related-party status alone does not prove diversion. The IPO raised₹40.1744 cr fresh gross, with₹9.2752 cr OFS going to sellers. Company expenses₹4.7713 cr exceeded allocation by₹.3558 cr, offset against GCP, leaving company net proceeds₹35.4031 cr. Annual-report use tables show the funds used, not still available as extra cash. The December 8, 2025 exchange clarification included the signed auditor certificate and legible results, so the missing-signature issue is resolved. Promoter-group ownership reported at March 2026 was 73.68%, but that is not freely tradable float. ESOP approval reserves 300, 000 shares; no option cash is assumed received. Legal concerns remain precisely qualified: JNPA's show-cause alleges omitted proceedings/project-count mismatch and warns of possible debarment, while management denies a material expected impact. The separate technical-eligibility challenge failed. The former employee's WP(ST)9850/2024 was dismissed on 10 September 2026 for non-prosecution, not on merits, superseding the old pending label. No final Alibag outcome or final JNPA show-cause order was located. These facts support conditional governance scrutiny, not a fraud verdict. [E10,E13–E19]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 revenue₹135.8631 cr, reported PAT₹17.7461 cr and CFO₹9.3596 cr are the main-statement figures, not the contradictory AS7 table. Core operating EBITDA is₹19.7811 cr and EBIT₹19.4780 cr before a separately identified₹.1321 cr mutual-fund-loss addback. Other income₹5.2638 cr is mainly FD interest₹5.0986 cr. The₹1.3984 cr increase in FD interest explains 46.28% of₹3.0215 cr PBT growth; prior-year tax credit₹.2712 cr also helps PAT. Three-year CFO/PAT 57.83% and five-year 43.55% show persistent weak realization; FY26 CFO less PPE capex is₹8.7268 cr, but additional FD investment₹31.9787 cr makes that an incomplete owner-cash measure. Receivables₹43.9211 cr include₹4.7706 cr disputed considered-good balances, mostly over 3 years; WIP₹12.6891 cr and multi-year deposits add collection risk. Full main audit, IFC and audit-trail annexures are positive. CARO's bank-return agreement conclusion is absent, not an adverse reconciliation finding. Note 36 nevertheless reports zero AS7 revenue and negative profits equal to costs despite substantial main service revenue; clarification is essential. FD liens₹92.0983 cr exceed all book FD₹91.5379 cr by₹.5604 cr; none is casually netted against debt. FY25 comparative total assets rose₹.8719 cr from the prospectus through GST gross-up and liability regrouping, not higher earnings. EPS uses closing shares as weighted shares, an unresolved presentation issue; current-share EPS is correctly a separate valuation denominator. The multi-year financing-side capital bridge is independently reconciled to asset/liability movements, includes all uncertain cash/FD capital, and shows core and collateral-interest-inclusive returns. It is not project IRR and not a current-ROCE shortcut. [E06–E12,E20]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At the stale₹57 reference, equity value is₹125.99 cr, reported P/E7.10× and P/B 1.02×. A simple enterprise value that deducts all bank deposits would be misleading, so the primary model is an explicitly funded equity-earnings return model with a book-equity impairment cross-check. Recurring PAT includes earnings on retained required FDs and the applicable financing/guarantee costs; terminal equity adds only signed unrestricted cash above a₹3 cr operating reserve. No extra value is added for those FDs, operating property, or partnership assets. Capitalizing only FD income can substantially haircut collateral principal relative to its face value; this is conservative terminal monetization, not a claim that the principal disappears. The separate impaired book-equity cross-check retains that asset support. Persistent non-interest financing fees use the audited ₹1.1850 crore / FY26 sales ratio, approximately 0.8722%, even after OD repayment; lower and higher cost ratios are sensitivity cases, not unsupported base-case relief. All annual rows and sensitivities are included below/in the canonical record. The strict no-release cases cannot support non-rescue return targets. A separate conditional own-collateral conversion releases at most₹33.5348 cr after retaining BG/joint collateral and the mapping gap, repays₹13.185 cr OD once, settles old dues, and reduces future FD income. The base release case is funded and has an illustrative return computed in the table below, but that is not an ordinary forecast because the release right/timing and financial-note reliability are unverified. Bear and fast-growth bull release cases breach the reserve, so their non-rescue returns/entry prices remain null. Explicit rescue alternatives pre-fund all interval uses, pay 3% issuance fees and use whole shares at an assumed 20% discount; dilution is not hidden. Reverse exit-P/E requirements at 12/15/18% hurdles are solved only on verified funded brackets. No ordinary entry recommendation, R score or P score is asserted. Two-way working-capital/multiple, collateral/reserve, capex/prefund and margin/collateral stresses expose the dependencies. Execution-cost stress is separately shown and taxes remain before investor tax. [E07,E08,E11,E19,E22]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear case is not that repair demand vanishes. A concentrated government customer delays approval/payment while the company must keep labor, suppliers and performance guarantees funded. Lower bids or rework reduce margins; disputed old debtors do not collect, retentions roll forward, and bank collateral cannot be released in time. Tax litigation or a partial guarantee call adds cash demands. A low headline P/E then capitalizes income that cannot be distributed, and a discounted capital issue reduces per-share value. The explicit bear model links 12% initial revenue decline, 10.5% EBITDA margin, 43% ONWC intensity, 50% collateral intensity, lower FD yield and₹8.25 cr tax/partial-BG cash stress. This is a sensitivity, not a prediction that guarantees will be invoked. Conversely, substantial bank deposits, positive profit and the 2025 rating upgrade are real evidence against an imminent-default narrative. The thesis-break variable is dependable conversion of certified work and collateral into usable cash without repeated unfavorable financing. A proven material governance violation would separately change G1; an unresolved allegation does not. [E03,E07–E11,E15,E16,E22]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A multibagger label is not supported by the present evidence. Fivefold price appreciation over five years requires about 38.0% annualized price growth; tenfold requires 58.5%. The ordinary valuation case is not scoreable, and the fast-growth scenario itself strains funding before any stock-price multiple expansion. The algebra separates revenue, margin, share dilution and exit P/E: unchanged margin, shares and multiple require revenue to grow 5× or 10×, while every rescue or ESOP reduces the per-share result. Moving from roughly₹136 cr revenue to₹680 cr would require far more tender wins, execution staff and financial collateral than the stale₹193 cr backlog demonstrates. A larger repair market is not evidence that MRIL can capture and finance that scale. No precise success probability or speculative long-term target is assigned. Classification: unsupported on current evidence. [E04,E06,E19,E22]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Review with each filed result and material exchange announcement, not by automatically scheduling alerts. First, obtain an auditor/company correction of the AS7 zero-revenue table and FD-lien mapping; an unexplained repeat is a thesis-break for reliability. Second, track actual collection of the₹4.77 cr disputed receivables and>6 month₹8.06 cr balance; rising ageing without independently explained recovery weakens asset support. Third, reconcile free bank cash, deposits, OD renewals and the release conditions against known obligations before using any ordinary return estimate. Fourth, watch CFO/PAT over rolling three years against the 57.83% baseline and distinguish genuine collection from stretched subcontractor retentions. Fifth, request a dated executable-backlog bridge, customer concentration and cancellation/extension terms rather than an undated order figure. Sixth, compare actual revenue, debtor days and cash needs with the prospectus's unrealized planning estimates. Seventh, monitor remuneration and connected transactions relative to profit and cash generation. Eighth, track final JNPA/Alibag outcomes, distinguishing allegations, procedural closure and merits findings. Ninth, verify actual ESOP grants, exercise prices and new shares rather than the plan reserve alone. Tenth, recheck current lot/series, queues and observed whole-lot exit capacity. None of these analytical thresholds is an automated trading instruction. [E04–E22]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold—unresolved. Arithmetic BQS 4.52 indicates mixed/weak business quality, not severe proven governance failure; raw GQS 5.20 is capped 5.00 for persistent cash weakness. IAS remains NS with no ordinary hurdle-entry price because important financial-note and funding/market-execution evidence is unresolved. This is a research-priority value/special-situation case, not an eligible purchase and not an automatic sell instruction for a holder whose portfolio, taxes and execution constraints are unknown. A cheaper quote alone does not clear G2 or release collateral. The constructive path is specific: reconcile contract-revenue/cash notes, authenticate the ability to settle/release collateral, demonstrate improved collections and produce an updated executable order schedule. Only then can the apparently low valuation be assessed normally. No governance numeric override or actual-default finding has been applied. [E07,E10,E11,E15,E20–E22]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The source hierarchy is the complete FY26 exchange-filed annual report, final 18 August 2025 NSE prospectus, older DRHP for FY 22, dated rating rationales, and exchange ESOP/IPO clarifications. The final prospectus supersedes reliance on an RHP mirror. Court texts are explicitly labeled judicial reproductions on a secondary host; the short September 10 order was fully exposed in the search index, but no freshly downloaded official court PDF was available. All material historical inputs have page/section locators and original-document hashes where bytes were fetched. Model assumptions are analyst-created: 15% equity hurdle distinct from 14–18% capital-cost diagnostic, 3 cr cash reserve, seasonal 47%Q 4 allocation, mark-to-market/haircut of mutual funds, collateral-release mechanics, no assumed new debt limits, continuing guarantee costs, no future dividends, and conditional 6/9/12× exit PE. Neither private project IRRs nor current bank-release letters were available; meaningful aggregate incremental returns are still calculated rather than imputed. Open questions are the AS7 table, FD note overlap/accrual, weighted EPS, exact bank-return reporting, updated legal outcomes and current executable liquidity. [E01–E24]

summary: Mahendra Realtors is principally a structural-repair, rehabilitation, waterproofing and civil-works contractor, with legacy BOT/property exposures. It is not a conventional land-bank developer. The attractive surface story is a profitable contractor at about 7.1× FY26 profit and roughly book value. The decisive problem is that much of the apparent cash is project collateral, multi-year cash conversion is weak, and important notes do not reconcile. BQS is 4.5 and capped GQS 5.0; IAS is NS. This is a conditional value/special-situation research case, not an evidence-backed compounder or an eligible new-purchase recommendation. A clear auditor reconciliation, freely usable liquidity and demonstrably collectible contract assets would change the conclusion more than a lower headline P/E. [E01,E06,E07,E11,E22]
